papers.title: The Thermodynamic Complexity of Circuits
papers.abstract: When any physical system executes a logically irreversible (non-injective) step of a computation, the excess heat released over the Landauer limit is an energetic cost that cannot be recovered. In modern computers this cost vastly dwarfs the Landauer cost. Modern stochastic thermodynamics refers to this cost as the ``entropy production'' and has derived fundamental lower bounds on its value. Here we introduce a thermodynamic model of circuits using heat functions and investigate its entropy production, deriving new results on the thermodynamic complexity of circuits. We first show that computing the optimal heat functions for gates in a given circuit (minimizing the entropy production) is PP-complete and multiplicative approximation of those heat functions is NP-hard, but additive approximation admits a polynomial-time randomized algorithm. We give tight bounds for entropy production for certain specific families of circuits (on uniformly distributed inputs): an $n$-ary AND tree of depth $O(\log n)$ requires $\Omega(n)$ entropy production, while a serial chain achieves $O(1)$ in an idealized model, showing an energy-depth tradeoff. The Batcher odd-even mergesort network on $n$ bits has $\Theta(n)$ entropy production, asymptotically less than its $\Theta(n \log^2 n)$ gate count. On random permutations of distinct integers its entropy production is $\Theta(n \log^2 n)$, asymptotically exceeding the Landauer cost of sorting; but preceding it with Leighton and Plaxton's almost-sorting network reduces the total heat released to $O(n \log n)$. Finally, we show how to sort $n$ values with zero circuit entropy production over any exchangeable input distribution. Our framework also yields streamlined proofs of known results in stochastic thermodynamics on mismatch cost and modularity cost.

papers.title: Wave Is All You Need: A Quantum Language Model Based on Fully Connected Quantum Boltzmann Machine
papers.abstract: This work proposes a self-attention mechanism based on the fully connected quantum Boltzmann machine (FC-QBM), and further constructs a fully connected quantum Boltzmann machine language model (FC-QBM-LM) using the mechanism as the core engine. By performing unitary evolution on semantic quantum states, the mechanism implicitly implements positional encoding and self-attention computation, eliminating the need to decompose continuous semantic streams into discrete matrices for explicit matrix multiplication, with the measurement results naturally satisfying the normalization condition. Specifically, this work rigorously derives the computational principle of the self-attention mechanism based on FC-QBM, and demonstrates that this mechanism is mathematically equivalent to the classical self-attention mechanism. The mathematical principles governing the training and generation of FC-QBM-LM are thoroughly derived, and the two corresponding algorithms are subsequently developed. An 8-qubit FC-QBM-LM is finally constructed and trained on the corpus of Tang poetry. Under the 8-qubit setting, the quantum layer implements the entire positional encoding and self-attention computation pipeline with only 44 parameters. In the noiseless scenario, the model exhibits favorable convergence. Furthermore, the quantum circuit proposed in this work, which terminates with Y-axis rotation gates, achieves better convergence than the counterpart terminating with X-axis rotation gates. Under the small-sample regime and across eight distinct noise intensity levels, the model demonstrates strong noise robustness, retaining over 99% of its noiseless convergence performance. Experiments on five-character quatrain generation reveal that the model preliminarily exhibits three core capabilities: associative and divergent thinking, content generation across imagery and human-aligned word ordering.

papers.title: Generative AI in Turbulence: Foundations, Applications, Validations and Benchmarks
papers.abstract: Generative AI offers new approaches to turbulence problems in which incomplete observations or unresolved d.o.f. admit multiple physically plausible solutions. Potential applications include stochastic closures, super-resolution, data assimilation, uncertainty quantification, and the generation of Eulerian and Lagrangian flow ensembles. However, turbulence is not a conventional image-generation problem. Its multiscale dynamics, intermittency, extreme events, rough velocity fields and intrinsically stochastic transport make visual realism, pointwise error, and low-order spectral agreement insufficient measures of physical fidelity. We examine where generative AI provide novel capabilities with emphasis on diffusion models, score-based methods, and related probability-transport formulations. We discuss their use in unconditional generation, probabilistic reconstruction, reduced-order modeling, temporal evolution, and mesh-free representations. We argue that validation must address turbulence properties: energy transfer, structure functions, anomalous scaling, pdf tails, coherent structures, conservation laws, temporal consistency, ensemble diversity and generalization. Finally, we discuss potential limitations in validation, baseline, data availability and reproducibility, and the need for a benchmark ecosystem combining open data, standardized challenges, hidden tests, physics-aware metrics, and documented failures. This paper serves as a bridge between two communities. For AI practitioners, we provide a fair and accessible introduction to turbulence, essential for appreciating the challenges posed by the field and for assessing the physical relevance of generative models. For turbulent practitioners, we provide an introduction to the key technological aspects of Generative AI, clarifying what these tools actually do, and where their potential and current limitations lie.

papers.title: Optimality and annealing path planning of dynamical analog solvers
papers.abstract: Recently proposed analog solvers based on dynamical systems, such as Ising machines, are promising platforms for large-scale combinatorial optimization. Yet, given the heuristic nature of the field, there is very limited insight on optimality guarantees of the solvers, as well as how parameter schedules shape dynamics and outcomes. Here, we develop a dynamical mean-field framework to analyze Ising-machine dynamics for finding the ground state energy of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick(SK) model of spin glasses and identify mechanisms that enable rapid convergence to provenly near-optimal energies. For a fixed target energy density Ec, we show that solutions are typically reached within O(1) matrix vector multiplications, indicating constant time complexity. We further delineate theoretical limitations arising from different parameter-scheduling trajectories and demonstrate a pronounced benefit of temperature-only annealing for the Coherent Ising Machine. Building on these insights, we propose a general framework for designing optimized parameter schedules, thereby improving the practical effectiveness of Ising machines for complex optimization tasks. The superior performance of the dynamical solvers is illustrated by the attainment of the ground state energy of the SK model.

papers.title: Distributional statistics of nonequilibrium
papers.abstract: We establish a reference modeling framework for random probability distributions subject to constraints. Generalizing the hyperensemble approach of Crooks, we formulate Jaynesian priors of maximal uncertainty over the unit simplex of categorical distributions. This framework is entirely general, but we primarily investigate models with constraints on physically relevant quantities, namely, average energy and Shannon entropy. A constraint on the exact value of average energy uniquely determines a Boltzmann-Gibbs equilibrium, but also defines a hyperplanar subset of the probability simplex consisting of all distributions with that value of average energy. The associated hyperensemble has a uniform probability density across all such distributions, regardless of distance to equilibrium. Such reference models make predictions of generic nonequilibrium properties such as the mean and modal microstate distributions and the expected free energy of a random distribution, which we examine analytically and via exact sampling algorithms. Moreover, introducing constraints on Shannon entropy permits parametric access to tunably nonequilibrium regimes. The approach follows conventional Jaynesian modeling logic and is compatible with standard Bayesian inference, and reduces to Boltzmann-Gibbs statistics when Shannon entropy is maximized. We examine the physical predictions of this scheme, and demonstrate its wide compatibility with other approaches to nonequilibrium modeling. We illustrate the framework in three scenarios: (i) comparison to superstatistics quasi-equilibrium modeling, (ii) generation of random nonequilibrium steady states, and (iii) Bayesian inference under a prior hyperensemble. We highlight numerous prospects for theoretical extensions and empirical application.

papers.title: Machine learning kinetics from molecular dynamics data
papers.abstract: Most molecular transitions occur on time scales far beyond direct molecular dynamics simulations. The committor, the probability that a configuration reaches a product state before a reactant state, is a central kinetic statistic, providing a mechanism-independent reaction coordinate and a foundation for transition path theory and the calculation of rates. This review surveys modern approaches for estimating the committor and related kinetic statistics from molecular simulations, with an emphasis on self-supervised methods that learn solutions of their defining dynamical equations rather than relying on labeled shooting data. We develop a common operator viewpoint connecting generator-based partial differential equations, variational principles, Markov state models, dynamical Galerkin approximation, and neural networks. Empirical and theoretical evidence points to the efficiency of these methods. We provide theoretical and practical guidance for realizing their full potential in applications, including strategies for treating non-Markovian effects and for sampling. We conclude by identifying opportunities for further research, including connections to reinforcement learning and generative modeling.

papers.title: Local Koopman modes of saddle-point diffusions: exact singular functions and a data-driven estimator
papers.abstract: Coherent sets-regions of phase space that resist mixing-organize transport in stochastic dynamical systems and are encoded in the leading singular functions of the stochastic Koopman operator. These are typically computed numerically and globally; a local, analytic theory near a fixed point has been missing, although fixed points and the transitions between them organize the flow. We supply the local theory for a saddle, the transition state through which probability flows between basins. Naively the construction fails-probability escapes along unstable directions, the invariant measure is non-normalizable, the singular functions leave $L^2$, and singular values exceed one. We show that conditioning on non-escape (a Doob's $h$-transform) repairs this; that the required $h$ is the unique stabilizing solution of an algebraic Riccati equation; and that the resulting slow modes decay at the escape rate along the unstable manifold. We obtain these modes in closed form-products of Hermite polynomials in canonical coordinates times the $h$-function-and use their unitary structure to derive a data-driven estimator: canonical correlation analysis on conditioned trajectories. When a single unstable direction dominates, the leading mode is the reaction coordinate, locally recovering the stable manifold and committor of transition-path theory. The construction connects coherent sets to transition-path theory, to the stabilizing Riccati solution of linear control, and to the time-reversed dynamics of generative diffusion models.

papers.title: Occupation counts of rarely switching Markov chains: stratified local laws, support selection and the boundary layer
papers.abstract: A Markov chain with exit rates $q_i$ runs for $N$ steps with transition matrix $I+(T/N)Q$. On each irreducible face that carries start mass, we prove a local limit theorem for the occupation counts with an explicit constant and relative error $O(1/T)$, uniformly for $1\le T\le\varepsilon N$ with $\varepsilon\max_iq_i<1$ and on compact subsets of the open face. Up to $O(1)$, minus the log-probability of counts $n$ with support $F$ is $|F|-1$ times $\log(N/\sqrt T)$ plus $N$ times the Donsker and Varadhan functional of $I+(T/N)Q$ at $n/N$. Every admissible face has an explicit power of $T$ in its largest probability for large $T\le N^{1/3}$, and a constant given by a finite-dimensional variational formula. For $T=\tau\log N$ the face of the mode minimizes $\tau\lambda_F+|F|-1$ at first order, with $\lambda_F$ the exit rate. If an admissible face has $\Delta\ge1$ more states than another and an exit rate smaller by $\delta>0$, we locate every crossing of their largest probabilities for large $T\le N^{1/3}$ up to $O(1/\log N)$. For two irreducible faces the crossing is unique for large $N$ in $1\le T\le\varepsilon N$, with coefficient $1/2$ of $\log\log N$. Near a facet, the continuous-time occupation density is the facet density times an explicit kernel, with relative error $O(1/T)$ at times $x\le cT$ off the facet, $c$ small. The counts obey a lattice form with extra error $T^2/N$ for $T\le\varepsilon_1\sqrt N$. The kernel is Bessel for $x=o(T)$ at facet profiles where the removed state has equal entry and exit laws, and at a profile where the rate has a first correction, of order $m\ge3$, if and only if $x=o(T^{1-2/m})$. On the complete graph with the uniform start, each face of at least 2 states crosses a vertex exactly once.

papers.title: Linear statistics in the Coulomb gas: cumulants beyond rotational invariance
papers.abstract: We consider a classical Coulomb gas of $N$ particles in dimension $d\geq2$, confined by a general external potential $U$ in the large-$N$ limit. In that limit the density of particles has a compact support called the droplet. We study smooth linear statistics ${\mathcal L}_N=\sum_{i=1}^N f({\bf x}_i)$ at large $N$. While the leading variance of ${\mathcal L}_N$ is by now well understood in many settings, much less is known about higher cumulants. When $f({\bf x})=f(|{\bf x}|)$ and the potential is rotationally invariant, these cumulants were computed recently at leading order. We derive explicit formulas for the leading third and fourth cumulants for general smooth droplets, without assuming that either the potential or the test function is radial. The answers are expressed as intrinsic boundary integrals over the equilibrium droplet. The third cumulant depends on the cube of the jump of the normal derivative of the harmonic extension of $f$, while the fourth cumulant also involves the exterior Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator, the mean curvature of the boundary, and normal derivatives of the background density. Our derivation uses the tilted potential $U_s=U+s f/\beta$, the associated deformation of the droplet, and shape derivatives of the Dirichlet energy. This deformation has a natural interpretation as the infinitesimal motion of the free boundary in the obstacle-problem formulation of the equilibrium measure. Our formulas extend previous studies by Wiegmann and Zabrodin in two dimensions for $\beta=2$. In their setting, we provide a rigorous proof of the limiting third and fourth cumulants, supporting the proposed formulas for general Coulomb gases. We specialize the general formulas to the disk, the half-plane and the sphere, and check them against exactly solvable non-radial deformations, including translated elliptic droplets in $d=2$ and spheroidal deformations in $d=3$.

papers.title: Boundary-condition independence of infinite-chain ground states in the $S=1$ $J$-$D$ antiferromagnetic chain
papers.abstract: Extending the analytic machinery and using the numerical inputs from OpenAI's proofs of the Haldane gap, we study infinite-chain ground states of the $S=1$ $J$-$D$ antiferromagnetic model $H=\sum_j\{\boldsymbol S_j\cdot\boldsymbol S_{j+1}+D(S_j^{\mathrm z})^2\}$ for sufficiently small $|D|$. We consider two finite-volume settings: periodic chains with an even number of sites, and open chains with an odd number of sites and the same positive magnetic field in the $\mathrm z$ direction at both endpoints. We prove that the ground states in each setting have an infinite-chain limit along the full sequence, without passing to a subsequence, and that the two limiting states coincide. Convergence is uniform in $D$ on a fixed neighborhood of zero. The common limit is a symmetric locally-unique gapped ground state, and its local expectation values depend continuously on $D$. These conclusions concern the two specified constructions, not uniqueness among all infinite-chain ground states. They provide the input for the study of a topological phase transition in a forthcoming revision of our companion paper. The author formulated the problem and proposed the basic strategy. ChatGPT Astra made substantial contributions to the inductive estimates and to completing the proof.

papers.title: Large spin large deviations for interacting particle systems
papers.abstract: We propose a novel framework for analyzing the sample-path large deviations of interacting particle systems directly on a lattice by considering a large-spin limit ($s \to \infty$). Through an appropriate scaling of variables, the process concentrates around its deterministic trajectory, governed by the lattice diffusion equation. We quantify the exponential cost of observing atypical trajectories by explicitly computing the path-space large deviation rate function from the scaled microscopic generator, based on a theory due to Feng and Kurtz. The rate function is described in terms of a Hamiltonian on a lattice in terms of classical spin variables. Notably, for our main model, the symmetric harmonic process, the corresponding Hamiltonian is identified with the classical integrable non-compact Ishimori spin chain. Furthermore, we show that our large spin large deviation theory is fully consistent with traditional Macroscopic Fluctuation Theory (MFT), smoothly recovering the standard MFT Hamiltonian in the spatial continuous limit. We also perform a Poisson-noise Martin--Siggia--Rose (MSR) computation to derive the non-linear lattice Hamiltonian directly from microscopic dynamics, use a relative entropy argument to obtain the density-current action, and establish the lattice fluctuation theorem alongside its symmetry origin. Overall, our framework provides a naturally regularized, lattice analogue of MFT that circumvents spatial ultraviolet singularities and possible continuous density blow-ups. We also apply our new scheme to partial symmetric exclusion process, symmetric inclusion processes, Brownian energy process and integrable heat conduction model, showing how their large-deviation Hamiltonians relate to classical compact and non-compact spin chains.

papers.title: Path space large deviation on a lattice for interacting particle systems
papers.abstract: We investigate the path space large deviation principle (LDP) for a class of interacting particle systems on a fixed finite discrete torus. As an illustrative example, we use the partial exclusion process with maximal occupation of $s$ particles. We first verify the standard Kurtz-type law of large numbers for the original and tilted processes, thereby identifying the deterministic flows around which the large deviations are formulated. We then establish the path space LDP, with speed $s$, and identify the associated rate function in variational form as the Legendre transform of a nonlinear Hamiltonian. The proof relies on martingale techniques, exponential tightness, and a change-of-measure argument based on exponential tilting, which renders atypical trajectories typical under a modified dynamics. We also explain how the same strategy extends to further interacting particle systems. The inclusion process illustrates the conservative non-compact finite-jump case. The harmonic process is qualitatively different: a single transition may move a variable number of particles, and the limiting Hamiltonian is logarithmic with a non-trivial domain. This places the harmonic process outside the usual finite-reaction framework for density-dependent Markov jump processes. Finally, we discuss continuous-state energy-exchange models, such as the Brownian energy process and an integrable heat-conduction model, to indicate how the same Hamiltonian large-deviation formalism appears beyond discrete-state particle systems.

papers.title: Trajectory Functionals in the Thermodynamics of Radiation-Induced Damage in Structural Materials
papers.abstract: This paper delivers a novel self-consistent non-local kinetic framework based on dose-dependent semi-Markov renewal transport and the generalized Doob's h-transform to evaluate the structural degradation of WWER-1000/1200 fuel claddings. By leveraging the Feynman-Kac formalism, we map the continuous microscopic defect path trajectories generated by the Liouville operator directly onto the evolution of the macroscopically integrated damage potential. The framework accounts for long-range memory effects in the degradation kinetics via a non-vanishing structural commutator of the path Liouville operator and Zwanzig-Mori projection operators, which mathematically links the spatial restrictions of microscopic sinks to energetic path penalties. Spatial profiling of the cladding's mean lifetime, demonstrates a distinct sigmoidal, S-shaped degradation trajectory encompassing distinct incubation, linear growth, and avalanche breakdown stages. The numerical results reveal an abrupt, localized reduction in the operational lifespan near the cladding boundaries. This marginal vulnerability is shown to be a direct physical consequence of boundary stress field singularities at the fuel cladding interface and localized embrittlement. The developed path integral architecture provides a strict thermodynamic link between non-equilibrium fluctuations and the global Griffiths macro-barrier, offering a robust predictive tool for high-burnup nuclear fuel safety assessments.

papers.title: Maximization of nuclear fusion reactivity via optimal energy distributions
papers.abstract: We investigate the optimization of nuclear fusion reactivity relative to the choice of energy probability distribution. A single Maxwell-Boltzmann (MB) distribution is found to be optimal in the region where reactivity is a concave function of the average available kinetic energy, specifically near the reactivity peak. Conversely, in regions where the reactivity curve is convex, optimization is achieved through a bimodal MB distribution. We then discuss our results in the context of three classes of generalized energy distributions (superstatistics), which are modeled as a continuum of MB distributions. As expected, in all cases examined, the reactivity gains provided by superstatistics are bounded by the proposed optimal distribution. Finally, we apply these findings to deuterium-deuterium and deuterium-tritium fusion processes using empirical parametrizations of their respective cross sections. For both reactions, employing optimal bimodal MB distributions at low average energies-of particular interest for magnetically confined plasmas-yields a reactivity enhancement of approximately a factor of 2.

papers.title: Random Matrix Spectra from Boltzmann-Weighted Lattice Ensembles
papers.abstract: We introduce a random matrix framework for studying statistical-mechanical lattice systems through spectral observables. Equilibrium configurations sampled from a Boltzmann measure are mapped to matrix ensembles whose covariance structure is inherited from the spatial correlations of the underlying model. This construction maps real-space correlation functions to a momentum-space variance profile, providing a direct bridge between statistical-mechanical correlations and correlated random matrix ensembles. We derive this variance profile in finite-correlation-length and critical regimes, and compute spectral moments within a Wick-contraction expansion. A complementary self-consistent description of the bulk density is developed using the resolvent formalism. These analytical methods are benchmarked against Monte Carlo data for the two-dimensional Ising model and three-dimensional Edwards--Anderson spin glasses. In both cases, the spectra evolve from the semicircle law at high temperature to model-dependent critical forms reflecting the structure of correlations. The framework, therefore, provides a quantitative spectral route to probing collective behavior in ordered and disordered statistical systems, while also defining a class of physically motivated correlated random matrix ensembles.

papers.title: Absence of hidden analytic conserved quantities in harmonically confined rods
papers.abstract: Systems of hard rods of equal length in a one-dimensional harmonic trap have been observed to exhibit peculiar non-ergodic behavior that might suggest the existence of a novel hidden conserved quantity beyond the two well known ones, i.e., the total energy and the center-of-mass energy. In this work, we investigate this possibility by systematically constraining the forms of the conserved quantities, and we rigorously rule out the existence of any extra hidden conserved quantity that is analytic in the positions and momenta of the rods involved. We do so by showing two key results: conservation during free motion demands the $U(1)$ invariance of these quantities under rotations of the position and momenta of each rod, and conservation during collisions demand an $S_N$ invariance under the permutation of the momenta of the rods as long as one of the rods have non-zero length. We then show that these conditions imply that any conserved quantity is functionally dependent on the two known conserved quantities. In addition, we show that in the special case where all rods have zero length (i.e., when they are point particles), conservation under collisions only requires invariance under a smaller $S_N$ group of permutations of the labels of the rods, which leads to a much larger set of analytic conserved quantities that we explicitly write down. In all, this rigorously clarifies the structure of conserved quantities in the hard rod problem, and motivates the application of such systematic methods to other classical systems.

papers.title: A Simple Necessary and Sufficient Condition for Yang--Baxter Integrability
papers.abstract: Quantum integrability is a cornerstone of the exact theory of interacting quantum spin chains. In its standard formulation, however, one starts from R-matrices satisfying the Yang--Baxter equation, rather than from the Hamiltonian itself. It has therefore remained unclear how Yang--Baxter solvability can be characterized directly at the Hamiltonian level, and how it is related to the existence of local conservation laws. Here we prove that, in a broad standard setting, the Reshetikhin condition is not only necessary but also sufficient for Yang--Baxter integrability, thereby reducing the hidden algebraic structure of integrability to a Hamiltonian-level conservation law. Since the Reshetikhin condition is equivalent to conservation of the total energy current, this Hamiltonian-level criterion is also experimentally accessible. This result establishes a quantum counterpart of the Liouville--Arnold theorem for isotropic spin chains, stating that Yang--Baxter solvability is equivalent to an infinite hierarchy of local conserved quantities. Our result also simplifies substantially the search for integrable spin chains by replacing the search for R-matrices with a direct criterion on local Hamiltonians.

papers.title: Turning angle analysis reveals hidden anisotropies in intracellular transport
papers.abstract: Molecular motion within living cells provides a window into the physical principles underlying intracellular organization and transport. Yet a fundamental limitation remains: measured trajectories are often short, noisy, and randomly oriented, rendering spatial anisotropies inaccessible to conventional analyses. We show that turning-angle statistics provide a robust approach for uncovering anisotropies in anomalous diffusion. Using a two-dimensional anisotropic fractional Brownian motion model with random orientations, we show theoretically and through simulations that turning-angle distributions preserve signatures of anisotropy. We apply this approach to single-particle tracking data, including quantum dots in the cytoplasm of HeLa cells and membrane proteins in hippocampal neurons. Turning angles reveal hidden anisotropies in the motion of quantum dots and Kv1.4 channels, and in specific dynamical states of glycoprotein CD4. These results establish turning-angle analysis as a powerful strategy for detecting organization in complex environments and reveal that anisotropic anomalous diffusion is an {often} overlooked feature of intracellular dynamics.

papers.title: OpenFerro: a unified framework for mesoscale ferroic dynamics and enhanced sampling
papers.abstract: Modeling ferroic materials requires connecting microscopic fluctuations to collective dynamics over mesoscales. We introduce OpenFerro, a unified lattice-field dynamics framework that combines flexible Hamiltonians, automatic differentiation, parallel execution, and enhanced sampling. The same framework can simulate ferroelectric domain motion, magnetic disordering, and coupled spin-lattice thermodynamics. On four graphics processors, a bulk BaTiO$_3$ benchmark with long-range dipolar interaction reaches $840^3$ unit cells, representing 3 billion atoms through the retained lattice variables. We simulate polarization textures in a PbTiO$_3$/SrTiO$_3$ superlattice spanning $0.8~\mu\mathrm{m}$ laterally and a BaTiO$_3$ nanoparticle 200~nm in diameter, retaining unit-cell resolution. We also demonstrate enhanced-sampling simulations that reconstruct the polarization free-energy surface of bulk BaTiO$_3$ without a prescribed polynomial form. With moderate computational resources, OpenFerro achieves atomistic-resolution simulations at mesoscopic scales traditionally studied with continuum models.

papers.title: Virtual defect mediated quantum melting in supersolids
papers.abstract: The current understanding of supersolid melting is largely based on mean-field theories predicting that such transitions arise from a structural energy minimization mechanism. Here, we show that soft-core quasi-one-dimensional supersolids stabilized by a shallow external lattice can instead melt at zero temperature into a superfluid phase with quasi-long-range positional order through the proliferation of virtual soliton--antisoliton pairs, leading to a Kosterlitz--Thouless transition. We derive the corresponding Renormalization Group equations from first principles and use them to determine the critical properties of the system. Remarkably, the proliferation of topological defects near criticality strongly renormalizes both the density modulation and the superfluidity behavior. The transition described is intrinsically a beyond mean-field effect, since the external lattice produces only a smooth crossover between weakly and strongly modulated states at the mean-field level.

papers.title: Learning by Confusion Locates a Parametrization-Dependent Fisher Information Maximum
papers.abstract: Learning by confusion (LBC) is a machine-learning method for locating phase transitions without assuming a known order parameter. Its characteristic accuracy curve contains a central maximum that is interpreted as the transition point, but what determines the location and finite-size scaling of this maximum has remained unclear. We derive an exact balance condition for the Bayes-optimal confusion peak and show that, for equilibrium systems with a single swept parameter, the peak closely follows the maximum of the corresponding Fisher information. This immediately gives its finite-size scaling and reveals an unexpected dependence on how the data are sampled: the same configurations arranged on grids uniform in $T$, $\ln T$, or $\beta=1/T$ can yield different finite-size pseudocritical trajectories. Tests on the Ising, Blume-Capel, Potts, and Baxter-Wu models confirm the prediction across continuous, tricritical, and first-order transitions. Our results identify the statistical quantity measured by LBC and show that finite-size machine-learning estimates can depend on the parametrization of the training data as well as on the underlying physics.

papers.title: Quantum state revivals, time quasicrystals, and entanglement steering in a Fibonacci-driven central-spin model
papers.abstract: Motivated by the search for non-equilibrium phases of matter beyond the Floquet paradigm, we propose a route to realize perfect revivals and time quasicrystals (TQCs) in a Fibonacci-driven central-spin model with Ising interactions between the central and satellite spins in the absence of disorder. We analytically demonstrate that when the interaction strength, $\lambda$ is tuned to $2 m \pi$, no entanglement is generated between the central and satellite spins at stroboscopic times, independent of the strength of the transverse driving field and the drive sequence. This leads to indefinitely long-lived quasiperiodic oscillations in satellite spin magnetization. Furthermore, for initial states with a definite bath magnetization, no entanglement is generated when the transverse driving field, $\theta$ is tuned to $\pi$ for any value of $ \lambda$, and the satellite spin magnetization oscillations exhibit period-3 revivals at Fibonacci times. Examining the robustness of these oscillations away from this fine-tuned limit, we identify a parameter regime where the quasiperiodic response does not decay over the timescales probed, giving rise to a long-lived $\pi$-pulse-proximate TQC regime. We further show that at special Clifford points, the system exhibits perfect quasiperiodic oscillations of the satellite spin magnetization, with a parity-dependent Fourier response. This response persists over the timescales probed, even away from the Clifford points for an even number of satellite spins, leading to the formation of a Clifford-proximate TQC. Finally, we demonstrate that at this Clifford points, the system is steered along an entangled trajectory, leading to the dynamical generation of Bell-cat and spin-cat states. These states exhibit magnetization of collective spin fluctuates quadratically with the number of satellite spins, thereby enabling Heisenberg-limited metrology.

papers.title: Intrinsic Hamiltonian of Mean Force and Strong-Coupling Quantum Thermodynamics
papers.abstract: We present a universal thermodynamic framework for quantum systems strongly coupled to thermal reservoirs, identifying the class of initial conditions required for consistent thermodynamic behavior. Unlike other approaches, our framework provides a unified description of both thermodynamic processes and thermostatic properties, while preserving the same gauge freedoms as in the standard weak-coupling regime and retaining the von Neumann expression for the thermodynamic entropy. Furthermore, the formulation is entirely in terms of the system's reduced state, relying only on variables accessible through local microscopic control. It is therefore directly connected to experimentally accessible quantities, making it possible to address operational questions concerning the controlled system-such as determining the minimum work required to drive it between two prescribed states in the presence of a strongly coupled reservoir. We validate our approach using a paradigmatic model of a structured bosonic reservoir.

papers.title: Deep Thermalization and Measurements of Quantum Resources
papers.abstract: Quantum resource theories provide a unified framework for characterizing useful quantum phenomena subject to physical constraints, but are notoriously hard to assess in experimental systems. In this letter, we introduce a unified protocol for quantifying the resource-generating power of arbitrary quantum evolutions applicable to multiple resource theories. It is based on deep thermalization, which has recently gained attention for its role in the emergence of quantum state designs from partial projective measurements. Central to our approach is the use of projected ensembles, recently employed to probe deep thermalization, together with new twirling identities that allow us to directly infer the resource-generating powers of the underlying dynamics. These identities further reveal how resources build up and thermalize in generic quantum circuits. Finally, we show that quantum resources themselves undergo deep thermalization at the subsystem level, offering a complementary and another experimentally accessible route to infer the resource-generating powers. Our work connects deep thermalization to resource quantification, offering a new perspective on the essential role of various resources in generating state designs and on efficient estimation of quantum resources in experiment.

papers.title: Fate of Quantum Scars and Chaos-Assisted Tunneling under Dissipation
papers.abstract: Quantum scars enable memory and recurrent dynamics, but their fate under dissipation remains poorly understood. Here, we show that distinct quantum scars can respond qualitatively differently to the same dissipative channel. We consider a collective spin model coupled to a lossy cavity and, guided by its classical limit, identify scars associated with two unstable structures: a saddle point on a dissipation-free invariant manifold with vanishing cavity field and an unstable superradiant fixed point with finite photon occupation. The former is immune to photon loss in the classical limit and exhibits persistent quantum revivals, whereas the latter couples directly to the dissipative channel, but exhibits slow dynamics. Remarkably, the superradiant scar also supports chaos-assisted quantum tunneling between two symmetry-related, macroscopically distinct semiclassical configurations, despite the presence of dissipation. Our results identify an experimentally accessible setting for exploring dissipative scarring and chaos-assisted tunneling in cavity QED.

papers.title: Effective Hamiltonian description on monitored Majorana chains: correlated power-law hoppings and unconventional entanglement scaling
papers.abstract: We investigate the structure of effective Hamiltonians governing monitored dynamics of a one-dimensional Majorana chain using Lyapunov spectral analysis. We focus on the gapless phase of the Lyapunov spectrum, where the effective Hamiltonians behave differently from conventional critical Hamiltonians in isolated systems; the spectral gap closes faster than $1/L$ but slower than $1/L^2$ and the entanglement entropy grows as $[\ln(L)]^2$ where $L$ is the system size. We find that the effective Hamiltonians have random long-range power-law hoppings with nontrivial magnitude correlations, rather than being independently and identically distributed. To elucidate the role of these non-Gaussian correlations, we construct random power-law hopping models that capture the essential features of the effective Hamiltonians. The spectral gaps of the constructed models decay faster than $1/L$ but slower than $1/L^2$. We find that, in the absence of hopping correlations, the ground-state entanglement exhibits $\ln(L)$ scaling. In the presence of correlations, by contrast, the entanglement entropy is enhanced and its system-size dependence is consistent with $[\ln(L)]^2$ scaling over the system sizes studied. These results suggest that correlations among long-range hopping magnitudes are responsible for the entanglement scaling rarely encountered in the ground states of conventional isolated quantum systems.

papers.title: The Ising lattice gas and the surface diffusion of CO on Cu(001) at finite coverage
papers.abstract: The memory equation of the coherent intermediate scattering function (ISF), derived previously for lattice gases, is applied to the Ising lattice gas under Kawasaki dynamics. The ISF follows the decay of a density wave of adparticles, a superposition of exponential relaxation modes: the decay starts at a rate fixed by a sum rule and is then slowed by a memory. The static structure factor and the effective hop rate are obtained in closed form, exactly along a one-dimensional channel; with the sum rule they give a single exponential, a lower bound on the ISF. Exact relaxation spectra show that this single exponential, built from equilibrium quantities alone, reproduces the correlation time only at weak coupling; only there can a measured dephasing rate be read through the statics. For strong attraction the slow dissolution of clusters lengthens the correlation time up to ninefold, whereas a repulsive layer relaxes nearly as a single mode at its structure peak. The dephasing rate, fitted over a time window where it is nearly constant, approaches the slowest relaxation rate, not the initial one; the sum rule reaches the data only through the area beneath the normalized decay, which defines the correlation time. For CO/Cu(001), the lattice gas reproduces the dephasing rates measured along two crystal directions and requires a nearest-neighbour repulsion of at least $35$--$50$~meV, whatever the jump rates; the measured rate is then close to the inverse correlation time, and the memory is predicted to grow with coverage.

papers.title: Optimal Search Strategies under Finite Resource Constraints
papers.abstract: Improving target search is a challenge faced by many natural and artificial agents, often requiring the use of energetic or material resources. These inputs may be supplied by an external controller or generated by the searcher itself, for example, through the deposition of cues along its trajectory. Although such resources are commonly modeled as costly but available without an explicit limit, in practice, they can often only be produced in finite amounts. Here, we go beyond the assumption of an unlimited supply of resources by investigating searches in which a finite resource budget must be allocated throughout the search process. To investigate this problem, we equip a one-dimensional diffusive searcher with three types of resources: an external force, a supply of partially reflecting flags, and auto-chemotactic cues. We derive exact optimal resource-allocation protocols for informed search processes in which the agent has continuous access to its past and current positions, which we find to always require resource allocation to be spatially concentrated. We then determine the corresponding protocols for blind searchers and show that resource usage must be more evenly distributed. Non-Markovian cues that generate environmental memory are found to substantially improve search performance when the agent has access to positional information, even under finite-resource constraints. In contrast, their benefits are considerably more limited for blind search, particularly when the cues provide no directional information.

papers.title: Jensen-Mercer two-sided bounds for entropy production rate
papers.abstract: Bounds on entropy production convert limited observations into constraints on hidden dissipation. The Jensen bound expresses a lower bound on the total and subsystem entropy production rates of continuous stochastic systems in terms of mean coordinate rates alone. We show that the same convexity structure yields a complementary upper bound, inspired by Mercer's reflection inequality. For the quadratic entropy-production functional of overdamped Langevin dynamics, Mercer's reflection inequality is identical to the sharp Bhatia-Davis variance bound and coincides with the convex dual of the smallest affine majorant of the functional over the range of the local current. The two bounds yield a two-sided sandwich controlled solely by the mean drift and the extrema of the current, organized into a hierarchy of optimal bounds in which each further observation tightens the ceiling. The thermodynamic uncertainty relation supplies an independent fluctuation floor. We also treat position-dependent diffusion, underdamped dynamics and the tilted periodic potential, for which the weak-barrier series is obtained in closed form and the strong-barrier regime is solved asymptotically. We check the bounds numerically on the Brownian motor.

papers.title: Information geometry of continuum limits in lattice field theory: The Gross-Neveu model with Wilson fermions
papers.abstract: When the Boltzmann weight is nonnegative, the actions of a lattice field theory define a family of probability distributions that forms a statistical manifold, and its Fisher metric gives the number of measurements needed to distinguish two nearby actions. In the large-$N$ limit of the two-dimensional lattice Gross-Neveu model with Wilson fermions, we study the continuum limit, in which the lattice spacing $a$ is taken to zero with the mass gap $\Lambda$ fixed, through the Fisher metric of the distribution of the auxiliary field $\sigma$. The renormalization condition fixes an expectation coordinate, and dimensional transmutation becomes an exponential relation between it and a natural coordinate. The main result is that the $a\to0$ limits differ between the Fisher metric of the long-distance modes, whose momenta are fixed in physical units, and the Fisher metric of the full $P(\sigma)$. In the former, the lengths of the infinitely many irrelevant directions that change the kinetic term shrink, relative to the mass-term direction, to order $a\Lambda\log(1/(a\Lambda))$ or smaller, and when several modes are combined, only the two directions $(\Lambda,m)$ of the continuum theory remain. In the latter, the kinetic-term directions shrink at the same rate as the mass-term direction, and the difference in the regularization remains in correlations at distances of the order of the lattice spacing. An exception is the deformation that only adds a contact term to the propagator: as $a\to0$ its length goes to zero in both metrics, and it becomes indistinguishable from a change of the coupling $1/g^2$ (a lattice version of Kutasov's result). The curvature of the coupling plane at fixed kinetic term diverges as $(1/2)\log^2(1/(a\Lambda))$, not as the correlation volume often assumed in thermodynamic geometry, and the critical point is infinitely far in Fisher distance from any point at finite $a$.
